is doc-engine opensource

Yes, doc-engine is an open source project. It is a high-performance headless document layout and vector rendering engine built for React and TypeScript. It allows for the creation of searchable vector PDF 1.7 streams and 60 FPS HTML5 Canvas previews without requiring headless browsers or server-side daemons.

what about layer

Layer is an open-source tool designed to bridge the gap between AI coding agents and large-scale codebases. It serves as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides AI agents with symbol outlines, exact function slices, and impact graphs instead of raw file dumps.

It solves the issues of excessive token usage, hallucinated APIs, and broken refactors by using Tree-sitter for instant syntax checking and plugging into real toolchains (like tsc or cargo) for verified diagnostic feedback.

Tech Stack: Rust.
GitHub: https://github.com/junaidmirr/layer

It features constant-time symbol lookups, atomic indexing to prevent lock contention, and task-aware context ranking to optimize agent performance.
how to install layer in my macbook

To install Layer on your MacBook, you should visit the GitHub repository at https://github.com/junaidmirr/layer. As it is written in Rust, ensure you have the Rust toolchain installed via rustup. You can clone the repository and build the binary directly from the source using cargo build --release. Once built, you can integrate the executable with your preferred Model Context Protocol (MCP) enabled AI agent, such as Cursor or Claude Code, by pointing the agent configuration to the local binary path. Detailed build and configuration instructions are provided in the repository's README.

messages.content: Tell me about doc-engine

doc-engine is a high-performance headless document layout and vector rendering engine designed for React and TypeScript. It solves the issue of bloated, server-heavy PDF generation by calculating layout coordinates in pure TypeScript and emitting native vector PDF 1.7 operators and 60 FPS HTML5 Canvas previews locally.

Key stack: TypeScript, React 19, HTML5 Canvas, and native PDF 1.7 spec implementation. It features automatic pagination, real-time rendering, and avoids heavy dependencies like Puppeteer or Python daemons. It is published as an npm package (@worklabs05/doc-engine).

GitHub: https://github.com/junaidmirr/doc-engine.git
